work.work-title: The Road and the Miles tae Dundee

credit.credit-words: The Road and the Miles tae Dundee

direction-type.words: Verse3:At once she consented and gave me her airm. Nae a word did I spear fa that lassie micht be.
She appeared like an angel in feature and form, as she walked by my side on the road tae Dundee.
Verse4:At length wi' the Howe o' Strathmartine behind us, the spires o' the toon in full view we could see.
She said 'Gentle sir, I can ne'er forget ye, for showin' me sae far on the road tae Dundee."
Verse5:"This ring and this purse please accept as a token, and surely there's something that ye can gie me?
That in the years tae come, I'll remember the laddie, fa showed me the road and the miles tae Dundee."
Verse6:Sae I took the gaud pin fae the scarf on my bosom, and I said "Tak' ye this in remembrance o' me."
And bravely I kissed the sweet lips o' that lassie, ere I pairted wi' her on the road tae Dundee.
